_about: Boeing (McDonnell Douglas), DC/MD-10 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (DAC-67803A, reprinted January 1991, Revision A April 2004; boeing.com's airport planning page, DC10.pdf, 2023), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions, Model DC-10 Series 30 and 30CF (Lower Galley) (page index 13): side, plan and front views on one sheet, a 1-bit scan on graph paper (about 27.5 px a meter at scale 4). layers.py --mode image --unrotate --rotate 180 at scale 4, clip 120,300,505,434 (stored page points). Pixels of that raster, line centres. Started from the MD-11's placed points (md11/) moved by plug.py (3.0 m out at 15 m and 3.68 m at 40 m, scaled 1.0463 along and 1.0217 up), then the fuselage's tail, the fin, the tail engine and the wing engine placed here. The fuselage's tail cone ends under the tail engine at the printed 51.97 m, where the dimension's extension line starts (1409, 355): crown and belly are bridged to it (hidden) from 1340 and 1400 px, where the tailplane's side outline crosses them. The wing's CF6-50 nacelle hides the belly from its inlet to its exhaust (hidden). The fin stands on the tail engine's nacelle: its leading edge from the nacelle's top (1222, 216) to the top's front (1395, 44), its trailing edge from the fairing behind it (1400, 208) to the top's back (1470, 48); the rudder's hinge line is fin.rudder. The tail engine: inlet at 1131, the cowl's top to its end at 1435 (tailCowlEnd), the fairing over the nozzle from the fin's trailing edge back to 1495, the nozzle and its plug to 1508 (tailExhaust). The tailplane's side outline crosses the tail cone (not traced: plan and front).
